keywords.def: calculate; decide on it after doing calculations
a number which is a guess but an acceptably accurate approximation
condition of not having enough water in your body so that you feel ill or weak
sign or feeling in the body showing the presence of an illness or a condition

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Beth. Nowadays, I often see people carrying water bottles with them to make sure they drink enough.
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Beth。现在，我经常看到人们随身携带水瓶，以确保喝够水。

sentences.en: How much water do you drink a day, Phil?
sentences.zh: Phil，你一天喝多少水？

sentences.en: Oh, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe about a litre? OK. And do you know how much water you should drink a day?
sentences.zh: 大概一升吧？好的。你知道你一天应该喝多少水吗？

sentences.en: I think it's probably about two litres. Ah, well, the number many people have heard is two litres a day.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是两升吧。啊，很多人听说过的数字确实是一天两升。

sentences.en: Of course, everyone needs to drink some water - over half the human body is made up of it.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都需要喝水——人体的一半以上都是由水组成的。

sentences.en: But exactly how much water do we need to stay healthy?
sentences.zh: 但我们究竟需要多少水来保持健康呢？

sentences.en: That's what we'll be discussing in this programme, along with some useful new vocabulary as well.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在本期节目中要讨论的内容，同时还会学到一些实用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And speaking of vocabulary, remember you can download all the new words and phrases from this programme, plus worksheet exercises to help you learn them, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 说到词汇，别忘了你可以从我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 下载本节课的所有新单词和短语，以及帮助你学习这些内容的练习页。

sentences.en: Great! But first I have a question for you, Phil.
sentences.zh: 太棒了！但首先我有一个问题要问你，Phil。

sentences.en: I mentioned that over half the human body consists of water, but there's an even higher percentage of water in our blood.
sentences.zh: 我提到人体的一半以上由水组成，但我们血液中的水分比例甚至更高。

sentences.en: But how much? Is our blood: a) around 80% water? b) around 90% water? or, c) 100% water?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是多少呢？我们的血液是：a）大约80%是水？b）大约90%是水？还是 c）100%是水？

sentences.en: I think it's around 80% water. OK, I will reveal the correct answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 我觉得大约80%是水吧。好的，我将在节目后段揭晓正确答案。

sentences.en: Our blood needs water so it can carry nutrients to the body's cells and organs.
sentences.zh: 我们的血液需要水来将营养物质输送到身体的细胞和器官。

sentences.en: The amount recommended is often given as two litres a day.
sentences.zh: 建议的饮水量通常是每天两升。

sentences.en: But why? Here to discuss this with BBC World Service programme, The Food Chain, is biologist, Professor John Speakman: So, I'm not sure how it was arrived at but it seems to be a number that has taken grip on a very large number of countries.
sentences.zh: 但为什么呢？BBC世界频道节目《食物链》（The Food Chain）请来生物学家John Speakman教授来探讨这个问题：所以，我不太确定这个数字是怎么得出来的，但它似乎成了在很多国家都根深蒂固的一个数字。

sentences.en: So, if you look at government recommendations around the world, they're pretty much all the same.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你看看世界各地的政府建议，它们几乎都是一样的。

sentences.en: They pretty much all say everybody's got to be drinking two litres of water.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎都说每个人都必须喝两升水。

sentences.en: Professor Speakman doesn't know how the number of two litres a day was arrived at – how it was decided or calculated.
sentences.zh: Speakman教授不知道每天两升这个数字是怎么得出来的——也就是它是如何被决定或计算出来的。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the idea of drinking two litres a day has taken grip on many governments around the world.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，“每天喝两升”这个观点已经在全球许多政府中根深蒂固。

sentences.en: When you say an idea has taken grip on something, you mean it's taken control of it.
sentences.zh: 当你对某种观点说它“taken grip”（扎根/占主导地位）时，意思就是它已经占据了控制地位。

sentences.en: Yes, Professor Speakman says that pretty much all governments are giving pretty much the same recommendation.
sentences.zh: 是的，Speakman教授说几乎所有的政府都给出几乎相同的建议。

sentences.en: He uses the phrase, pretty much to mean almost.
sentences.zh: 他用了“pretty much”这个短语，意思是“几乎”。

sentences.en: For example, 'pretty much all governments advise drinking two litres a day' means 'almost all governments advise it'.
sentences.zh: 例如，“几乎所有政府都建议每天喝两升”的意思就是“差不多所有政府都建议这样做”。

sentences.en: What Professor Speakman doesn't have, however, is any scientific evidence for this advice.
sentences.zh: 然而，Speakman教授没有的是这一建议的任何科学依据。

sentences.en: The number of exactly two litres isn't based on scientific fact, it's more of a ballpark figure – a number which is a guess, but which you still believe is approximately correct.
sentences.zh: 刚好两升这个数字并不是基于科学事实，它更像是一个“ballpark figure”（大致数字）——一个虽是猜测但你仍认为大致正确的数字。

sentences.en: Actually, the amount of water in our bodies is changing all the time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们体内的水量一直在变化。

sentences.en: Like your bank balance, which goes down when you spend money, your body loses water all the time, when you breathe, sweat, or go to the toilet.
sentences.zh: 就像你的银行账户余额在你花钱时会减少一样，你的身体在呼吸、出汗或上厕所时会一直在失水。

sentences.en: Exactly how much you need to drink depends on how much water your body needs to replace, and that mainly depends on your size.
sentences.zh: 你究竟需要喝多少水，取决于你的身体需要补充多少水，而这主要取决于你的体型。

sentences.en: But what happens when we drink less than we should?
sentences.zh: 但是，当我们喝的水比应喝的少时会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: Here's hydration expert, Dr Nidia Rodriguez-Sanchez, describing the effects of dehydration to BBC World Service's The Food Chain.
sentences.zh: 这位是补水专家Nidia Rodriguez-Sanchez博士，她向BBC世界频道的《食物链》节目描述了脱水的影响。

sentences.en: And also, many times we start getting dehydrated and we don't realise we are dehydrated.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候，我们开始脱水了，却并没有意识到自己脱水了。

sentences.en: So it's very common that we feel tired, or we feel, like, with a bit of a headache, or even we think we're hungry, and we go and get some food.
sentences.zh: 所以很常见的情况是，我们感到疲倦，或者觉得有点头痛，甚至以为自己饿了，然后去吃东西。

sentences.en: And actually what is happening is that we are thirsty, that we are dehydrated, we are starting to show some signs or some symptoms of dehydration.
sentences.zh: 但实际上发生的情况是，我们口渴了，我们脱水了，我们开始表现出脱水的一些迹象或症状。

sentences.en: Dr Sanchez describes the effects of dehydration, the condition of not having enough water in your body so that you feel ill or weak.
sentences.zh: Sanchez博士描述了脱水的影响，即体内水分不足以致于感到生病或虚弱的状况。

sentences.en: She mentions feeling tired, having a headache or a dry mouth as symptoms of dehydration.
sentences.zh: 她提到感到疲劳、头痛或口干是脱水的症状。

sentences.en: Symptoms are signs or feelings in the body showing the presence of some illness or condition.
sentences.zh: 症状是身体上显示某种疾病或身体状况存在的迹象或感觉。

sentences.en: So, whether you drink a little more, or a little less, it seems that around two litres of water a day is a good way to keep your blood and body healthy.
sentences.zh: 所以，不管你多喝一点还是少喝一点，每天喝两升左右的水似乎是保持血液和身体健康的不错方法。

sentences.en: Speaking of which, Phil, it's time to reveal the answer to my question, what percentage of our blood is water?
sentences.zh: 说到这儿，Phil，是时候揭晓我刚才问题的答案了，我们的血液中水分占多少比例？

sentences.en: You said 80%, and the answer is 90%. Our blood consists of around 90% water.
sentences.zh: 你说是80%，答案是90%。我们的血液大约由90%的水分组成。

sentences.en: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've used, starting with the phrase to arrive at a number, meaning to decide it by doing calculations.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回顾一下我们用过的词汇，首先是“to arrive at a number”（得出数字），意思是经过计算做出决定。

sentences.en: If an idea takes grip on something, it takes control of it.
sentences.zh: 如果一个观点“takes grip”（扎根），它就占据了主导地位。

sentences.en: The phrase pretty much means almost; for example, pretty much everyone likes chocolate, which means almost everyone likes chocolate.
sentences.zh: 短语“pretty much”意思是“几乎”；例如，“几乎所有人都喜欢巧克力”，意思就是差不多每个人都喜欢巧克力。

sentences.en: A ballpark figure is a phrase meaning a number which is an acceptably accurate approximation.
sentences.zh: “ballpark figure”（大致数字）这个短语的意思是一个可以接受的准确近似值。

sentences.en: Dehydration is the condition of not having enough water in your body so that you feel ill or weak.
sentences.zh: “Dehydration”（脱水）是指体内水分不足以致于让你感到生病或虚弱的状况。

sentences.en: And finally, a symptom is a sign or feeling in the body showing the presence of an illness or condition.
sentences.zh: 最后，“symptom”（症状）是指身体上显示某种疾病或状况存在的迹象或感觉。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. Why not join me now and head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, download the worksheet for this programme, and test yourself to see how much you remember?
sentences.zh: 我们的6分钟节目又到时间了。为什么不现在就加入我，前往我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，下载本节课的练习页，并测试一下自己记住了多少呢？

sentences.en: See you there soon! Bye!
sentences.zh: 回头见！再见！
